newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank declines weekend statement on Spiegel.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank declines weekend statement on Spiegel.

text.p: A Bundesbank official said on Saturday the German central bank will reserve comment until Monday on a magazine report saying Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer has asked whether European monetary union can be delayed.
The official at the Frankfurt-based central bank declined further comment.
Germany's Der Spiegel magazine said on Saturday that Tietmeyer had asked whether Germany and France could consider delaying European monetary union (EMU).
"Wouldn't it be a possibility, together with France, to agree to a delay in the start of the euro?" the magazine quoted Tietmeyer as saying in an article to be published on Monday.
Spiegel, citing unnamed sources, said Tietmeyer did not believe it would be wrong if currency union were delayed if Bonn and Paris did not meet the entry criteria this year.
A Spiegel spokesman said the magazine had not spoken directly with Tietmeyer, saying the information was based on talks with sources in Germany. He declined further comment.
